units.text: а.1) approval, on the submission of the Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation, of candidates for Deputy Chairmen of the Government of the Russian Federation and federal ministers, except the federal ministers referred to in point ‘д.1’ of Article 83 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation;
units.label: Point «а» Part 1 Art. 103 · “а.1) approval, on the submission of the Chairman of the…”

units.text: б) deciding the question of confidence in the Government of the Russian Federation;
units.label: Point «б» Part 1 Art. 103

units.text: в) hearing annual reports of the Government of the Russian Federation on the results of its activities, including on questions raised by the State Duma <21>;
units.label: Point «в» Part 1 Art. 103

units.text: г) appointment and removal of the Chairman of the Central Bank of the Russian Federation;
units.label: Point «г» Part 1 Art. 103

units.text: г.1) hearing annual reports of the Central Bank of the Russian Federation;
units.label: Point «г» Part 1 Art. 103 · “г.1) hearing annual reports of the Central Bank of the Russian…”

units.text: д) appointment and removal of the Deputy Chairman of the Accounts Chamber and half of its total number of auditors on the submission of the President of the Russian Federation;
units.label: Point «д» Part 1 Art. 103

units.text: е) appointment and removal of the Commissioner for Human Rights, who acts in accordance with federal constitutional law. The Commissioner for Human Rights may be a citizen of the Russian Federation who permanently resides in the Russian Federation and holds neither foreign citizenship nor a residence permit or other document confirming a citizen of the Russian Federation's right to permanent residence in a foreign State. In the manner established by federal law, the Commissioner for Human Rights is prohibited from opening or holding accounts (deposits) or keeping cash and valuables in foreign banks located outside the territory of the Russian Federation;
units.label: Point «е» Part 1 Art. 103

units.text: ж) declaration of amnesty;
units.label: Point «ж» Part 1 Art. 103

units.text: з) bringing charges against the President of the Russian Federation with a view to removal from office or against a President of the Russian Federation who has ceased exercising powers with a view to deprivation of immunity.
units.label: Point «з» Part 1 Art. 103

units.text: 2. The State Duma adopts resolutions on matters assigned to its jurisdiction by the Constitution of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 103

units.text: 3. Resolutions of the State Duma are adopted by a majority of the total number of its deputies, unless the Constitution of the Russian Federation provides for another decision-making procedure.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 103

units.text: <21> Part 1 was supplemented with a new point ‘в’, and the letter designations of subsequent points were changed, in accordance with the Law of the Russian Federation on an Amendment to the Constitution of the Russian Federation No. 7-ФКЗ of 30 December 2008, ‘On the Supervisory Powers of the State Duma in Relation to the Government of the Russian Federation’, which entered into force on the date of its official publication, 31 December 2008 (Rossiyskaya Gazeta, 2008, 31 December).
units.label: Art. 103 · “<21> Part 1 was supplemented with a new point ‘в’, and the…”

units.text: Article 103.1
units.label: Art. 103.1

units.text: The Federation Council and the State Duma are entitled to exercise parliamentary oversight, including sending parliamentary inquiries to heads of state bodies and local self-government bodies on matters within the competence of those bodies and officials. The procedure for parliamentary oversight is determined by federal laws and the rules of procedure of the chambers of the Federal Assembly.
units.label: Art. 103.1 · text

units.text: Article 104
units.label: Art. 104

units.text: 1. The right of legislative initiative belongs to the President of the Russian Federation, the Federation Council, senators of the Russian Federation, deputies of the State Duma, the Government of the Russian Federation and legislative (representative) bodies of constituent entities of the Russian Federation. The Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation and the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation also have the right of legislative initiative on matters within their jurisdiction.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 104

units.text: 2. Bills are submitted to the State Duma.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 104

units.text: 3. Bills on the introduction or abolition of taxes, exemption from their payment, issuance of state loans, changes to the State's financial obligations, and other bills providing for expenditure covered by the federal budget may be submitted only if accompanied by an opinion of the Government of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 104

units.text: Article 105
units.label: Art. 105

units.text: 1. Federal laws are adopted by the State Duma.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 105

units.text: 2. Federal laws are adopted by a majority of the total number of deputies of the State Duma, unless otherwise provided by the Constitution of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 105

units.text: 3. Federal laws adopted by the State Duma are submitted to the Federation Council for consideration within five days.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 105

units.text: 4. A federal law is deemed approved by the Federation Council if more than half of the total members of that chamber vote for it, or if the Federation Council does not consider it within fourteen days. If the Federation Council rejects a federal law, the chambers may establish a conciliation commission to resolve the disagreements, after which the federal law is subject to reconsideration by the State Duma.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 105

units.text: 5. If the State Duma disagrees with the Federation Council's decision, the federal law is deemed adopted if, on a repeat vote, at least two-thirds of the total number of deputies of the State Duma vote for it.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 105

units.text: Article 106
units.label: Art. 106

units.text: Federal laws adopted by the State Duma on the following matters are subject to mandatory consideration by the Federation Council:
units.label: Art. 106 · “Federal laws adopted by the State Duma on the following matters…”

units.text: а) the federal budget;
units.label: Point «а» Art. 106

units.text: б) federal taxes and levies;
units.label: Point «б» Art. 106

units.text: в) financial, currency, credit and customs regulation, and currency issuance;
units.label: Point «в» Art. 106

units.text: г) ratification and denunciation of international treaties of the Russian Federation;
units.label: Point «г» Art. 106

units.text: д) the status and protection of the state border of the Russian Federation;
units.label: Point «д» Art. 106

units.text: е) war and peace.
units.label: Point «е» Art. 106

units.text: Article 107
units.label: Art. 107

units.text: 1. An adopted federal law is sent to the President of the Russian Federation for signature and promulgation within five days.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 107

units.text: 2. The President of the Russian Federation signs and promulgates the federal law within fourteen days.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 107

units.text: 3. If the President of the Russian Federation rejects a federal law within fourteen days of its receipt, the State Duma and the Federation Council reconsider it in the manner established by the Constitution of the Russian Federation. If, on reconsideration, the federal law is approved in its previously adopted wording by a majority of at least two-thirds of the total number of senators of the Russian Federation and deputies of the State Duma, it must be signed by the President of the Russian Federation within seven days and promulgated. If, within that period, the President requests the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation to review the constitutionality of the federal law, the time limit for signing it is suspended while the Constitutional Court considers the request. If the Constitutional Court confirms the constitutionality of the federal law, the President signs it within three days of the Constitutional Court's relevant decision. If the Constitutional Court does not confirm its constitutionality, the President returns it to the State Duma unsigned.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 107

units.text: Article 108
units.label: Art. 108

units.text: 1. Federal constitutional laws are adopted on matters provided for by the Constitution of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 108

units.text: 2. A federal constitutional law is deemed adopted if approved by a majority of at least three-quarters of the total number of senators of the Russian Federation and at least two-thirds of the total number of deputies of the State Duma. An adopted federal constitutional law must be signed by the President of the Russian Federation and promulgated within fourteen days. If, within that period, the President requests the Constitutional Court of the Russian Federation to review the constitutionality of the federal constitutional law, the time limit for signing it is suspended while the Constitutional Court considers the request. If the Constitutional Court confirms the constitutionality of the federal constitutional law, the President signs it within three days of the Constitutional Court's relevant decision. If the Constitutional Court does not confirm its constitutionality, the President returns it to the State Duma unsigned.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 108

units.text: Article 109
units.label: Art. 109

units.text: 1. The State Duma may be dissolved by the President of the Russian Federation in the cases provided for by Articles 111, 112 and 117 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 109

units.text: 2. If the State Duma is dissolved, the President of the Russian Federation sets an election date so that the newly elected State Duma meets no later than four months after the dissolution.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 109

units.text: 3. The State Duma may not be dissolved on the grounds provided for by Article 117 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation within a year after its election.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 109

units.text: 4. The State Duma may not be dissolved from the time it brings a charge against the President of the Russian Federation until the Federation Council adopts the corresponding decision.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 109

units.text: 5. The State Duma may not be dissolved while martial law or a state of emergency is in effect throughout the territory of the Russian Federation, or during the six months before the expiry of the President of the Russian Federation's term of office.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 109

units.locator: CHAPTER 6. GOVERNMENT OF THE RUSSIAN FEDERATION
units.text: CHAPTER 6. GOVERNMENT OF THE RUSSIAN FEDERATION
units.label: CHAPTER 6. GOVERNMENT OF THE RUSSIAN FEDERATION

units.text: Article 110
units.label: Art. 110

units.text: 1. Executive power in the Russian Federation is exercised by the Government of the Russian Federation under the overall direction of the President of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 110

units.text: 2. The Government of the Russian Federation consists of the Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation, Deputy Chairmen of the Government of the Russian Federation and federal ministers.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 110

units.text: 3. The Government of the Russian Federation directs the activities of federal executive bodies, except those whose activities are directed by the President of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 110

units.text: 4. The Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation, a Deputy Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation, a federal minister or another head of a federal executive body may be a citizen of the Russian Federation who has reached 30 years of age and holds neither foreign citizenship nor a residence permit or other document confirming a citizen of the Russian Federation's right to permanent residence in a foreign State. In the manner established by federal law, the Chairman and Deputy Chairmen of the Government of the Russian Federation, federal ministers and other heads of federal executive bodies are prohibited from opening or holding accounts (deposits) or keeping cash and valuables in foreign banks located outside the territory of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 110

units.text: Article 111
units.label: Art. 111

units.text: 1. The Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation is appointed by the President of the Russian Federation after the State Duma approves the candidacy.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 111

units.text: 2. The President of the Russian Federation submits a candidate for Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation to the State Duma no later than two weeks after a newly elected President takes office or after the Government of the Russian Federation resigns, or within one week after the State Duma rejects a candidate for Chairman of the Government, or after the Chairman is removed from office by the President or resigns.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 111

units.text: 3. The State Duma considers the candidate for Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation submitted by the President of the Russian Federation within one week of the submission.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 111

units.text: 4. After the State Duma rejects the submitted candidates for Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation three times, the President of the Russian Federation appoints the Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation. In that event, the President is entitled to dissolve the State Duma and call new elections.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 111

units.text: Article 112
units.label: Art. 112

units.text: 1. No later than one week after appointment, the Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation submits proposals to the President of the Russian Federation on the structure of federal executive bodies, except where the previous Chairman was removed from office by the President of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 112

units.text: 2. The Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation submits candidates for Deputy Chairmen of the Government of the Russian Federation and federal ministers to the State Duma for approval (except the federal ministers referred to in point ‘д.1’ of Article 83 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation). The State Duma decides on the submitted candidates no later than one week thereafter.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 112

units.text: 3. Deputy Chairmen of the Government of the Russian Federation and federal ministers whose candidacies have been approved by the State Duma are appointed by the President of the Russian Federation. The President may not refuse to appoint Deputy Chairmen of the Government of the Russian Federation or federal ministers whose candidacies have been approved by the State Duma.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 112

units.text: 4. After the State Duma rejects three times candidates for Deputy Chairmen of the Government of the Russian Federation or federal ministers submitted under part 2 of this Article, the President of the Russian Federation may appoint Deputy Chairmen and federal ministers from among the candidates submitted by the Chairman of the Government. If, after the State Duma rejects three times the candidates submitted under part 2 of this Article, more than one-third of the positions of members of the Government of the Russian Federation remain vacant (excluding the federal ministerial positions referred to in point ‘д.1’ of Article 83 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation), the President may dissolve the State Duma and call new elections.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 112

units.text: 5. In the case provided for by part 4 of Article 111 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation, and where the State Duma is dissolved in accordance with the Constitution of the Russian Federation, the President of the Russian Federation appoints Deputy Chairmen of the Government of the Russian Federation and federal ministers (except those referred to in point ‘д.1’ of Article 83 of the Constitution of the Russian Federation) on the submission of the Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 112

units.text: Article 113
units.label: Art. 113

units.text: The Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation organizes the work of the Government of the Russian Federation in accordance with the Constitution of the Russian Federation, federal laws, and decrees, executive orders and instructions of the President of the Russian Federation. The Chairman bears personal responsibility to the President of the Russian Federation for the exercise of the powers vested in the Government of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Art. 113 · text
